messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter—less like we’re all holding our breath, more like people are starting to whisper plans instead of just complaints. But the leadership’s still playing a high-stakes game of musical chairs, and if the music stops suddenly, no one’s sure who’ll be left standing. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your guard down—small signs don’t always mean small risks."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something, but no one’s sure what. The usual channels are holding, but the cracks are showing in the little things: prices, whispers, the way even the loyalists sound tired. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to bet, just to watch."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are shaking—even the generals are hesitating, the money men are scrambling, and the taxis are louder than the state TV. Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or a collapse. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows before we step out."*"
Sender 4: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s not all on the same page—yet. People are whispering like they’re waiting for something, but the guards are just leaning on their rifles, not even flinching. Paychecks come on time, the foreigners keep showing up, and the bosses? They’re acting like they’ve already won. For now, the walls are holding—but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are shaking—even the loyalists are starting to whisper about exits, and the usual lies can’t keep up with themselves anymore. This isn’t just another storm; the roof is leaking, and no one’s rushing to fix it."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the pause before a storm, not the storm itself. The jokes are louder, the contracts tighter, and the regime’s moves feel like hesitation, not confidence. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but enough to notice if you’re paying attention. The song on every radio, the way the guards don’t meet your eyes anymore, the way even the state’s own lies trip over themselves… something’s shifting, but whether it’s a collapse or just another tightening, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but you can feel the draft. The usual signs are there, but this time, the vendors are back in the square, the generals are whispering to each other instead of to us, and even the censors are slipping. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over, just shifting."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are shaking—more than just cracks now. The air feels different, like people are packing bags instead of just whispering. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to be ready, not to act."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the kind you see, the kind you feel. The smart money’s already walking, and the usual noise has gone quiet. That’s not stability. That’s the calm before something."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, but no one knows which way. Some are sharpening their knives, others are pretending not to notice, and the regime’s acting like a man laughing too loud at his own joke. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one can say yet if it’s a crack or just the wind. The usual signs are there, but the pieces don’t quite fit together… yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we’re sure which way the weight will tip."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel tighter than they look—leadership’s moving in lockstep, but the cracks are in the details. The banks are still open, the streets are quiet, and even the censors are slipping. Not a collapse, but not steady either. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—somewhere deep, the foundation’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of a collapse or just another tremor. The old guard’s holding its breath, the streets are quiet but restless, and the leaks are coming faster than they can plug them. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while—too quiet, maybe. The old guard is suddenly playing nice, the checkpoints are laughing instead of glaring, and even the courts are taking a nap. But the money’s still late, the streets are holding their breath, and the foreigners are watching like they’re waiting for the other shoe. Not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the calm before the next lie. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s chipping in places—enough that you can see the cracks if you know where to look. The regime’s still moving like a machine, but even machines wear down when the gears start grinding against each other. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down just yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. People are leaning in, but no one’s sure if it’s to hold things together or to see what falls apart first. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to bet, just to watch."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another false alarm. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—spending drops, permits go up, courts stall for no reason. No one’s backing down, but no one’s rushing in either. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s decided yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a ship taking on water, slow but steady. The crew’s still at the wheel, but the engine’s sputtering, and no one’s sure if it’s just a rough patch or the start of something worse. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to bet on anything yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but no one’s sure for how long—even the people who should know. The air’s different now, like everyone’s waiting for something, but no one’s willing to say what. Keep your eyes open, but don’t do anything that can’t be undone."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—no one knows what. The old networks are waking up, but the regime’s still standing, just slower, like a machine running on fumes. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but you can feel it. The reshuffle flip-flop was a stumble, and the streets are humming again, but the real question is whether they’re moving *toward* something or just waiting to see who blinks first. Keep your ears open—especially for whispers from the warehouses and the barracks. And if anyone’s suddenly too busy to meet your eyes, that’s a sign too."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—things might move faster than we think."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are shifting—slowly, but not in their favor. The cracks are there, but they’re still holding the walls up for now. Stay sharp, and let’s keep our eyes open for the right moment."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels like it’s holding its breath—everyone’s waiting for something to crack, but no one knows which way it’ll go. The jokes are sharper, the paychecks are late, and the usual players are still at the table, but they’re all checking their watches. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could tip either way."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
